title: VirtualJoystick: theme colors should be white by default, not black
body:
### Tested versions

4.7-dev2 (new feature)

### System information

Godot v4.7.dev2 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9571) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

My request is to simply change the default colour from black to white.

(Note sure if this counts as a feature request but it isn't a whole new feature, just a straightforward change to an existing one.)

VirtualJoystick defaults to showing a black circle outline with a black filled circle in the middle. While it is possible to supply fully custom textures, this is a bit of a hassle given that the default is perfectly fine for most use cases, except that it is black, and I don't see any way to change its colour.

If the default texture were _white_ instead of black, then it would be possible to use the [`modulate`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_canvasitem.html#class-canvasitem-property-modulate) property to change it to any colour, even black (because it multiplies `modulate` by the pixel value of 1.0). But because it is black, `modulate` does nothing (because it multiplies by 0.0).

(Even disregarding the modulate thing, I feel like white is a more common colour for a virtual joystick in most games.)

Providing an explicit colour property would also satisfy the use case (and maybe make it a bit more obvious how to customize the colour), but `modulate` gets the job done if the base image is white.

Changing it to white would be a breaking change, so it would be good to do it during the 4.7 branch before this feature gets seriously used in many projects.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a VirtualJoystick.
2. Try to change its colour. The only way I can find to do this is create and load up a custom image.
